accueil.question: What is Imizi Links?
accueil.reponse: Imizi Links is a free community platform for people from East Africa who live in France or have just arrived. It brings together three services, namely mutual support between members to find reliable information about settling in, job and internship offers shared on behalf of partner companies, and events where people can meet. A blog completes the picture with practical guides to help you understand each step.

accueil.question: Who is Imizi Links for?
accueil.reponse: Anyone from East Africa (Burundi, Rwanda, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and neighbouring countries) who lives in France or is about to move here, whether you are a student, a young professional, a family or someone changing career. The community is also open to people who simply want to contribute, even if settling in is not something they are going through themselves.

accueil.question: Do Imizi Links services cost anything?
accueil.reponse: No. Every service is free, whether you ask for support, get in touch with a local contact, apply for a job we share, attend an event or read our guides. Imizi Links is run by volunteers and never charges its members.

accueil.question: Which cities does Imizi Links cover?
accueil.reponse: Volunteer local contacts are active in Paris and the Île-de-France region, Lyon, Bordeaux, Marseille, Lille, Toulouse and Nantes. If your city is not on the list, write to us and we will look for someone in your area or point you to the nearest city.

accueil.question: How do I join the Imizi Links community?
accueil.reponse: Each need has its own form. Use the Support page to ask for information or guidance, the Events page to sign up for an event, the Apply button on the Opportunities page to apply for a job, and the Join us page to become a local contact, contribute or ask a general question. There is no registration or membership fee.

accueil.question: Can Imizi Links give me information about a proof of accommodation?
accueil.reponse: A proof of accommodation (attestation d’hébergement) is written and signed by the person who actually hosts you. Imizi Links does not issue this document, but we explain which document you need to provide, and a local contact in your city can guide you if needed.

accueil.question: How long does it take to get a reply?
accueil.reponse: Support requests receive a reply from a local contact within 48 working hours. Job applications are passed on to the partner company within 72 hours. Other messages are handled within a few days.

entraide.question: Can Imizi Links give me information about a proof of accommodation?
entraide.reponse: A proof of accommodation (attestation d’hébergement) is written and signed by the person who actually hosts you. Imizi Links does not issue this document, but we explain which document you need to provide, and a local contact in your city can guide you if needed.

entraide.question: Who are the Imizi Links local contacts?
entraide.reponse: They are community members who have lived in France for several years and volunteer to be available to newcomers in their city. They know the local organisations (prefecture, landlords, universities) and point you to the right people. They do not carry out procedures on your behalf and they do not replace a social worker or a lawyer.

entraide.question: What should I do first when I arrive in France?
entraide.reponse: In this order, validate your long-stay visa online within three months of arriving, open a French bank account, register with the French social security system, then choose a regular doctor (médecin traitant). Each step often depends on the previous one, which is why the order matters.

entraide.question: Can Imizi Links help me find accommodation?
entraide.reponse: We are not an estate agency and we do not offer housing. We do, however, explain the options available to you (CROUS student residences, private residences, flat shares, the Visale guarantee) and the scams to avoid, and a local contact in your city can share practical advice. You can also read our guide to student housing.

entraide.question: Is the support from Imizi Links confidential?
entraide.reponse: Yes. Your request is only shared with the local contact who answers it. No personal information is ever published, sold or passed on to anyone else.

entraide.question: I have just arrived and my French is still limited, can you help me?
entraide.reponse: Yes. Several local contacts speak Kirundi, Kinyarwanda, Swahili or English and can talk with you in your own language. Simply mention it in your message.

opportunites.question: How do I apply for a job shared by Imizi Links?
opportunites.reponse: Each job has an Apply button. It opens a dedicated form where you upload your CV and cover letter. Imizi Links receives your application, checks it and passes it directly to the partner company. You do not need to contact the employer yourself.

opportunites.question: Why apply through Imizi Links rather than directly?
opportunites.reponse: The jobs listed here come from partner companies that have asked us to help with their recruitment. We present your application ourselves, which gives it more visibility than an application lost among hundreds of others. We can also give you feedback on your application before we send it.

opportunites.question: Which documents do I need to apply?
opportunites.reponse: An up-to-date CV and a cover letter, as a PDF, Word document or image. If you do not have a cover letter yet, you can still send your CV and we will get back to you to complete your application.

opportunites.question: Are the jobs open to international candidates or people whose residence status is being processed?
opportunites.reponse: Each job states the level required and the type of contract. Our partner companies know that candidates come from the community and are used to international profiles, including qualifications obtained abroad. Simply check that your residence permit allows you to work under the conditions offered.

opportunites.question: How long before I hear back about my application?
opportunites.reponse: We pass applications on to the partner company within 72 hours. After that, the response time depends on the recruiter, usually between one and three weeks. We keep you informed along the way.

opportunites.question: Can I apply for several jobs at the same time?
opportunites.reponse: Yes, there is no limit. Simply fill in one form per job so that each application reaches the right recruiter with the right cover letter.

opportunites.question: I represent a company, how can we publish a job on Imizi Links?
opportunites.reponse: Contact us at contact@imizilinks.fr. We review every request, introduce our pool of candidates and agree together on how applications will be passed on.

evenements.question: How do I sign up for an Imizi Links event?
evenements.reponse: Each event in the calendar has a Sign up button. It opens the registration form at the bottom of the Events page with the event already selected. You enter your name and email address, and we confirm your place by reply.

evenements.question: Do the events cost anything?
evenements.reponse: No, every event is free and open to all, whether it is a careers forum, a webinar, a workshop or a community evening.

evenements.question: Do I need to be a member to attend?
evenements.reponse: No. Our events are open to anyone who is interested, including people discovering Imizi Links for the first time. Some in-person events have limited places, so it is best to sign up in advance.

evenements.question: Where do the events take place?
evenements.reponse: In-person events mainly take place in Paris, Lyon and Bordeaux. Webinars and online workshops can be joined from anywhere in France and from abroad.

evenements.question: Can I organise an Imizi Links event in my city?
evenements.reponse: Yes, and we encourage it. On the Join us page, choose Organise an event in my city and we will help you with logistics, communication and connecting with members in your area.

evenements.question: What if I can no longer attend?
evenements.reponse: Let us know by email as soon as possible. For events with limited places, this frees up your spot for someone on the waiting list.

blog.question: Who writes the articles on the Imizi Links blog?
blog.reponse: Our guides are written by community members who have been through the procedures they describe themselves, sometimes reviewed by a local contact or a professional in the field. The aim is to share first-hand experience rather than rewrite official texts.

blog.question: Is the information in the guides up to date?
blog.reponse: We update the guides whenever procedures change. As the rules for settling in France change regularly, we always recommend checking official websites before taking an important step.

blog.question: Which topics does the blog cover?
blog.reponse: The steps involved in settling in France, such as the Campus France procedure, student housing, social security, opening a bank account and looking for work, as well as personal stories. New topics are added based on what the community asks for.

blog.question: Can I suggest an article or a topic?
blog.reponse: Yes. If you have been through a particular procedure or know a subject that would help the community, go to the Join us page and choose Write an article or a guide. We can help you with the writing if needed.

blog.question: Do the guides replace legal or professional advice?
blog.reponse: No. They are practical pointers based on real experience. For a complex situation (a refused residence permit, a dispute with a landlord, an employment dispute), please contact a qualified professional or a free legal advice service.

rejoindre.question: Which form should I use?
rejoindre.reponse: Each need has its own form with the right fields. Support requests go through the Support page, event registrations through the Events page and job applications through the Apply button on the Opportunities page. The form on the Join us page is for people who want to get involved, whether to become a local contact, write a guide, review CVs, organise a local event or ask a general question.

rejoindre.question: What happens to my personal data?
rejoindre.reponse: It is only used to handle your request. It is never sold, published or shared with anyone other than the person who answers you, or the partner company when you apply for a job.

rejoindre.question: How do I become an Imizi Links local contact in my city?
rejoindre.reponse: On the Join us page, choose Become a local contact in my city. We will then talk with you about your availability, the topics you can help with and how requests will reach you. There is no minimum commitment.

rejoindre.question: Can I contribute without being a local contact?
rejoindre.reponse: Yes. You can write a guide, review CVs, run a workshop, share a job from your company or organise a one-off event in your city. Every contribution counts, however much time you can give.

rejoindre.question: I represent an organisation or a company, how can we work with Imizi Links?
rejoindre.reponse: Write to us at contact@imizilinks.fr, or use the form on the Join us page and choose Share a job offer from my company or Organise an event in my city. We work with companies to share job offers and with organisations to run events.
